speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms first started and if they have been getting worse?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a significant injury. Can you describe exactly what you feel when you try to move the finger, and is there any visible deformity or bruising? REQUEST IMAGES: Right hand X-ray.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Extensor Lag of the Distal Interphalangeal Joint).

The injury mechanism (jerking pull), the inability to actively flex the DIP joint, and the finger resting in extension are classic signs of an extensor tendon rupture or bony avulsion at the distal phalanx. The X-ray requested previously will confirm if there is an avulsion fracture.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
